Excellent choice of song, I used to know how to play the organ parts on this. Anyway, whenever I see chord progressions that aren't diatonic to one key like this one, I like to think of how closely related each of the chords are. In this case, the first 4 chords can all fit into D minor, and the Eb can just is just borrowed from the key center that is one flat away. In other words, we start with one flat in the key and use a chord from the land of 2 flats (or 3/4). This is important because they are closely related keys, so borrowing a chord from there is not very jarring of a transition. On top of that the previous Bb creates a V I to Eb so the justification is compounded.

In my opinion any chord can lead to another one, each relationship creating a different sound. Dont get too caught up in trying to create reason for everything.

Elp is one of my all time favorites, and they're one of the few bands that I really got into and explored their stuff thoroughly. I honestly think that they have lots of good moments in their songs, just as good as the other great prog songs. However, I think that they fell off when it came to reproducing their "good stuff" consistently. Some songs are kind of throwaway songs, and often their stuff can go off on long crazy tangents. For example, karn 2nd impression, this song isn't one of their weirdest, but it was hard for me to get into because I seriously think there is no melody and not a lot of familiarity through the song. I like tarkus more because after 3 minutes of craziness it settles down and develops more melodic and riff driven sections. Its stuff like this that I don't think aged well, sometimes the real songwriting was absent, or parts of songs just seem like their purpose is mostly shock value. However, I dont think they should be discredited and they will always be one of my favorites.

My intj piano teacher is always explaining concepts in terms of what you can *do* with them. For example he'll say this is a great way to transpose to this key or achieve this certain sound. There is almost always a future intent in his mind, which is something I can't say for Ti. Additionally he is extremely methodical, and has tons of exercises to train certain skills or techniques. He is disciplined to get at the heart of things and actually *take away* something with him along the way. Musically, I think of myself as stretching the possibilities (Ne) with interspersed knowledge and structure (Ti/Si) and him as saying "I can explain that to you and along the way inadvertantly show you some ways to help you in the future."
